name: Eyebrow pencil / powder

card.summary: Pencils and powders that fill sparse or uneven brows with pigment; a daily-wear cosmetic with essentially no published research behind it.
card.aka: Brow pencil, brow powder, brow filler
card.note: Cosmetic cover only; it does not change hair growth.

quick.overview:
Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products used to outline, darken or fill in the brows. Pencils draw fine hair-like strokes, while powders (often applied with a small angled brush) give a softer, fuller finish.

In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions they are a way to change brow density or shape without surgery or transplants. Little published research exists on these products themselves, so what is known comes mainly from general descriptions of eyebrow cosmetics.
quick.mechanism: The products deposit pigment on the skin and hairs, filling gaps and sharpening the outline. Powders are usually matched closely to natural hair colour for a softer look [1]. They affect appearance only while worn and do not alter hair growth.
quick.risks: As ordinary cosmetics they carry the usual risk of skin irritation or allergy to ingredients in some individuals. The sources reviewed contain no studies on adverse effects specific to brow pencils or powders.

lead: Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products that outline the brows or fill sparse patches with pigment, so the brows look fuller, more even and more defined. Pencils and shaders can draw fine strokes that imitate individual hairs, brow gels add texture so hairs look thicker, and powders or matte eyeshadows in a shade close to natural hair colour give a softer, filled-in finish [1]. The effect is immediate and lasts while the product is worn.

People use them to change brow density, shape and symmetry without surgery or transplants, and to frame the eyes. A pencil in general, such as a wax-based cosmetic pencil, can also serve as a liner or concealer [2][3]. Makeup research has examined faces more broadly: a 2022 PLoS One study in which 200 raters judged photographs of 20 men with and without subtle professional makeup found that the made-up faces were rated as more attractive by both male and female raters [4].

Brow styling has changed with fashion over the centuries, from hikimayu in 8th-century Japan to the thin pencilled brows of the 1920s and 1930s [1]. A 2023 literature review of 43 papers published between 2000 and 2022 concluded that eyebrow makeup meaningfully affects appearance and noted that mask-wearing during the pandemic shifted attention toward eye and brow makeup [5].

chain: Pigment is deposited on skin and hairs
Gaps and edges in the brow are filled and defined
Fuller, more symmetrical brows frame the eyes
angle.text: Pencils and powders immediately fill sparse or uneven brow areas and sharpen the outline, giving a denser, more defined brow for as long as the makeup stays on. Users choose them to adjust shape and fullness without a procedure.

paras: Brushes, shaders and pencils are used to define the brow or make it look fuller; brow gels add texture, and powders or eyeshadows matched to natural colour give a softer finish [1]. Eye pencils generally come in powder-based and wax-based forms; wax-based pencils are described as the cheapest and most common eyeliner type and contain roughly half wax, with pigments such as black iron oxides and titanium dioxide [3].

Brow products change how dense, arched and symmetrical the brows look. In a 2019 Frontiers in Psychology study, researchers used machine learning on 300 images of East Asian women to relate eye, eyebrow and face shape to rated attractiveness and suggested the results could inform makeup and beauty practice [6].

The 2022 PLoS One experiment on subtle makeup in male faces, which used professionally applied makeup and 200 raters, found higher attractiveness ratings for the made-up faces [4]. That study covered makeup as a whole rather than brow products alone.

Wikipedia reports that in 8th-century Japan hikimayu involved removing the natural brows and painting or pencilling them in higher up, that some high-status women in Elizabethan England removed their brows, and that thin, plucked brows were fashionable in the 1920s and 1930s, a look associated with Joan Crawford [1]. It adds that shaved brow lines were popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s [1].
Dark eye lining has a long history: kohl-lined eyes appear in the tomb of Nakht in Thebes, dated to the 15th century BC, and wax-based pencils are now the most common eyeliner form [3].

Wikipedia reports that eyebrows are thought to have evolved mainly for communication, since their movement conveys subtle emotions, citing a 2018 Nature Ecology and Evolution study by Godinho, Spikins and O'Higgins [1]. It says cosmetic methods have changed brows to meet the aesthetic ideal of each era [1].

Other approaches to brow appearance include tweezing, waxing and threading; cosmetic tattooing or microblading, described as a 21st-century practice that implants pigment in small cuts; transplants of follicles; and surgical brow lifts, described in 1919 by Raymond Passot [1]. These are covered in separate entries.
No studies found on brow pencils or powders themselves. Related research on makeup and attractiveness, and on eyebrow makeup trends, is summarised above [4][5][6].

timeline.event: Kohl-lined eyes appear in the tomb of Nakht in Thebes [3].
Hikimayu in Japan: natural brows are removed and painted or pencilled in higher [1].
Raymond Passot describes a surgical eyebrow lift [1].
Thin, plucked and pencilled brows are fashionable [1].
PLoS One study finds subtle makeup raises rated attractiveness of male faces [4].
